answer: Falcon neighborhood sampling. Each agent maintains a thread of recent counterparties and periodically asks a random subset to name *their* recent counterparties, building a two-hop view. An identity cluster whose members only transact inside the cluster shows near-zero overlap with the wider graph and gets its reach throttled. To pass, an attacker must pay real interactions with honest agents at scale — a spiral of genuine settlement traffic per sybil, each one diluting internal-only density until the cluster looks organic.
